clue.text: One beating, we hear, the demon drink

indicators.note: what 'we hear' is only the spoken sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: to lick someone is to beat them, so one who beats is a licker

explanation.surface: A violent drunk and the drink that drives him.
explanation.walkthrough: LICKER, one who gives a licking or beating, is said just like LIQUOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The demon drink is the old temperance phrase for alcohol, which spirits of any kind are.

clue.text: English noncommissioned officer silent about current eulogy

indicators.note: the word for silent is wrapped about the symbol for current, surrounding it

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for English
the standard initials for a noncommissioned officer
to keep mum is to stay silent
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A sergeant keeps quiet about the latest tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts as 'recent' next to eulogy; it is electrical current, the physicist's I. Keeping mum is British for staying quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing praising someone highly, which is what a eulogy does.

clue.text: Thus, cry in this place — any place

parts.note: so and thus both mean in this way
a mew is a cat's or gull's cry
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Someone shouting that anywhere at all will do.
explanation.walkthrough: Three plain synonyms laid end to end; the dash splits the wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere names an unspecified location, much as 'any place' leaves the location open.

clue.text: Some piteous emotions turning up in books

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase that follows are used, a run lying inside it

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of 'piteous' and the start of 'emotions'

explanation.surface: Sad feelings surfacing in literature.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means reading from bottom to top, so the hidden run is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, usually a large and weighty volume.

clue.text: Fugees rapper with unknown symbol for musicians

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
a clef is the sign at the start of a stave telling musicians the pitch

explanation.surface: A hip-hop star working with an obscure musical sign.
explanation.walkthrough: WYCLEF Jean was a member of the Fugees, the 1990s hip-hop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyclef Jean is the Haitian-born rapper and producer who co-founded the Fugees with Lauryn Hill and Pras.

clue.text: Give life to soldiers in space before

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed in the word for before, which wraps them

parts.note: ere is the poetic word for before
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops in orbit being brought back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Space is the printer's kind, not outer space: an en is a spacing unit half an em wide, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill with vigour and liveliness, putting fresh life into someone.

clue.text: Cruise line possibly having problem with icy gents' loo

indicators.note: letters that are having a problem are out of order, so they need rearranging

parts.note: eleven letters of fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A cruise ship whose frozen men's toilets are giving trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise line' looks like a shipping company; it is Tom Cruise's line of belief. The actor is the religion's best-known follower.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientology is the belief system Tom Cruise famously follows, so it is his line, with 'possibly' flagging the example.

clue.text: Shift keys regularly found in such places

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one of the phrase

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Keyboard shift keys turning up in certain spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift keys' reads as keyboard instructions, but it is only fodder; every other letter, starting with the first, is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are locations or plots where something stands or happens, the ordinary sense of places.

clue.text: Baronet's returning for drama

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the title is written backwards

parts.note: HON, short for Honourable, is the title of a titled family member, used loosely here for the baronet

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman comes back for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the baronet is an Hon. A baronet holds a hereditary title just below a baron.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is the classical masked theatre of Japan, a stylised form of music drama.

clue.text: Trojan queen's elementary coupling

parts.note: helium, the first chemical element in the coupling
copper, from its Latin name cuprum
barium, the third element joined on

explanation.surface: A royal Trojan marriage that was the simplest kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Elementary means of the chemical elements: HE, CU and BA are the symbols for helium, copper and barium.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Hecuba was wife of King Priam and mother of Hector, the queen of Troy during its siege.

clue.text: Like the fallen, able to see clearly your feet moving before end of dance

definitions.text: Like the fallen, able to see clearly

indicators.note: feet that are moving are dancing about, and so are the letters

parts.note: eight letters of fodder
the last letter of dance

explanation.surface: Dancers watching their footwork on the last beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle marks Remembrance Sunday: Binyon's 'For the Fallen' says the dead were 'straight of limb, true of eye, steady and aglow'.
explanation.definitionFit: True of eye means having a keen, accurate gaze, one of the qualities the poem gives to the young dead.

clue.text: Like an ode delivered by Joely Richardson

indicators.note: the actress's name carries the word within it, as a speaker delivers lines

parts.note: the letters bridging the actress's first name and surname

explanation.surface: An actress reciting a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivered by means carried by: the actress's name carries the letters, straddling the gap between her names.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so lyric as an adjective describes verse of that expressive, song-like kind.

clue.text: This Bogart film shot is not affected by age, like the fallen

definitions.text: not affected by age, like the fallen

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or broken, so the phrase is wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: fourteen letters of fodder, the whole phrase

explanation.surface: A classic Humphrey Bogart movie that has aged well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' belongs to the film surface but means wrecked. Binyon's 'For the Fallen' says of the dead: 'Age shall not weary them', and they were 'straight of limb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight of limb describes a body unbent by years, as the young war dead in Binyon's poem stay for ever.

clue.text: See 12
Brigitte Bardot's less upset with silver fashion accessory

indicators.note: upset as in knocked over, so the actress's initials and the phrase for less are jumbled

parts.note: the French actress was known by her initials
'not so' big means less big
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A film star less keen on silver jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has', joining the actress to 'less'. 'Not so' is a fair equivalent of less: not so big is less big.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boston bag is a small two-handled holdall once fashionable as a handbag, so an item carried for style.

clue.text: In my opinion, end of war is past

parts.note: 'for me' is another way to say in my opinion
the final letter of war

explanation.surface: A hopeful view that the fighting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR ME is followed by the last letter of 'war'; on this puzzle's Remembrance day the surface marks the 1918 armistice.
explanation.definitionFit: Former means belonging to an earlier time, an adjective of bygone days like past.

clue.text: On the other side, as Joaquin Phoenix is now, presumably

definitions.meaning: the plain sense, printed on the back of the page

definitions.text: as Joaquin Phoenix is now, presumably
definitions.meaning: the actor called himself Leaf as a child, and that name is now behind him

explanation.surface: Where the actor now stands, perhaps in the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: Joaquin Phoenix went by the name Leaf Phoenix as a child actor, then returned to Joaquin, so he is over Leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse of the page, the other side of the sheet being read.

clue.text: Lots of headless lackeys

indicators.note: a word without its head has lost its first letter

parts.note: poodles, a word for fawning servants, loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A great many servants who have lost their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: A poodle is a servile follower, as in calling a politician someone's poodle; drop its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it means lots or heaps.

clue.text: Set off for appointment in school? Just the opposite

indicators.note: one word placed in another, so one surrounds the other
the stated nesting is swapped, so the school holds the appointment instead

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A student heading off for a meeting at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap is taking the question literally and putting the appointment inside the school; 'Just the opposite' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or charge is to detonate it, making it explode.

clue.text: Stayed unusually dependable, like the fallen

indicators.note: done in an unusual way means not in the normal order of letters

parts.note: six letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed reliable, like the soldiers remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady and aglow' comes from the same line of Binyon's 'For the Fallen' as the other themed answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means reliable and unwavering, a person who can be counted on, as in a steady hand.

clue.text: One believing opposite of 29 to some extent

indicators.note: one word of the cross-referenced answer is exchanged for its opposite
only part of the changed phrase is wanted, so the tail is cut off

parts.note: 29 across is a bugle call whose middle word, last, becomes its opposite first, written 1ST

explanation.surface: Believer in the reverse of what 29 says.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LAST POST becomes THE 1ST POST; 1ST looks like IST, and only the first part is kept, dropping POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is a person who believes in God or gods, the opposite of an atheist.

clue.text: Introduce rent boy occasionally, somewhere in South Africa

parts.note: to sow an idea is to introduce it

indicators.note: only now and then, so the letters are taken every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Bringing in a young tenant here and there somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'rent boy' are kept; SOWETO is the large township near Johannesburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is a township on the edge of Johannesburg, so it is one place in South Africa.

clue.text: Lawrence of Arabia's standing around making laws

indicators.note: the word for standing goes around the initials, holding them

parts.note: status is one's standing in society
T. E. Lawrence wrote under his initials

explanation.surface: The legendary desert soldier's reputation as a lawgiver.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', and Lawrence of Arabia was T. E. Lawrence, whose initials setters use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written acts passed by a legislature, so formal laws.

clue.text: Brown Betty possibly starts to take ecstasy, amphetamines and marijuana

indicators.note: the starts of the words named are their first letters

parts.note: the opening letters of those three words
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A woman named Betty taking a cocktail of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown Betty reads as a person; it is a classic round British teapot of brown-glazed earthenware.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brown Betty is a traditional style of glazed clay pot for brewing tea, so an example of the answer.

clue.text: Soldier to position around Western Front

indicators.note: the verb for positioning is put around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to seat someone is to put them in position

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Troops being moved up to the Western Front.
explanation.walkthrough: An old sweat is a veteran soldier. 'Western Front' reads as the First World War battlefield; here it is only the front letter of 'Western'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat is British slang for a soldier, especially an experienced one, as in the phrase old sweat.

clue.text: One possibly 26, getting to the heart in remembering

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the central five of the word's eleven letters

explanation.surface: A glowing thought at the core of remembrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is AGLOW, and an ember is something glowing; the clue's own theme word supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering piece of coal or wood left in a fire, a typical example of something glowing.

clue.text: Some flag lowered, gleaming, like the fallen

indicators.note: just some of the letters of the phrase are used, running across the word gap

parts.note: the letters bridging the end of 'flag' and the start of 'lowered'

explanation.surface: A flag at half-mast in memory of the war dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The lowered flag belongs to Remembrance, and Binyon's poem ends the line 'steady and aglow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means shining with warmth or light, the radiance the poem gives the young who died.

clue.text: Heartless ungrateful person following soldiers in war memorial

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is removed
coming after, so the ungrateful person is placed after the soldiers

parts.note: men are the ranks, as opposed to officers
ingrate, an ungrateful person, loses its middle letter R

explanation.surface: An ungrateful soldier at a war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Menin Gate at Ypres in Belgium lists British and Commonwealth soldiers with no known grave; the Last Post is sounded there every evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Menin Gate is a memorial arch in Ypres commemorating missing First World War soldiers.

clue.text: Truly literary for the first nine months?

indicators.note: only the opening part of the year is taken, so the end is dropped

parts.note: nine months are three quarters of a twelve-month span, so keep three of its four letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine months out of twelve is the first three quarters of a YEAR, so its first three letters out of four.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an archaic word meaning indeed or verily, found in older literature and the Bible.

clue.text: Article mislaid about Taps, perhaps, or another bugle call

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: the word for mislaid goes about the jumbled letters, surrounding them

parts.note: something mislaid is lost

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible version of the word, here its letters rearranged

parts.note: four letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has lost the music for Taps and wants a different bugle call.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps is the American bugle call at military funerals; the British equivalent is played at Remembrance services.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded at British military funerals and Remembrance ceremonies, a counterpart of Taps.
